sources.section: Public Knowledge Book: Muhammad Umar Farooq and Muhammad Soban
sources.text:
Source review date: 27–28 September 2026
Purpose: A human-readable, source-linked professional corpus for a future personal RAG.
Evidence rule: Use Umar's current portfolio as the preferred source for his education, experience, skills, and credentials; use his GitHub repositories and their READMEs as the authority for which public projects exist and how they work. Local Git/source review supports scoped internship and development-history facts. Results, deployment claims, awards, and credentials remain attributed claims unless an independent document or live test verifies them.
Scope: Professional and educational material from public profiles, user-supplied CVs, and Umar's user-identified local internship repositories. Local internship material is summarized at a professional level and is not presented as public GitHub work. Soban's supplied CV is treated as an attributed self-report; the CV file itself is not published here. Private journals, WhatsApp messages, Instagram chats, login credentials, and personal phone numbers are not included. This book has its own public-only index; it is separate from the general document-upload library.

The profile links explicitly associated with his portfolio, CV, or GitHub are GitHub (https://github.com/omerfarooq223), LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/in/omerfarooq223/), Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/omerfarooq223), Kaggle (https://www.kaggle.com/omerfarooq223), LeetCode (https://leetcode.com/u/OmerFarooq31/), and ORCID (https://orcid.org/0009-0002-3978-7448). His public professional email is momerfarooq223@gmail.com. Muhammad Umar Farooq is the name used in this book. The user accepts Omer, Omar, Umar, and Umer as spellings of his given name; Kaggle displays Muhammad Umer Farooq. These spellings refer to the same person.

sources.section: 3.5 Evidence-backed chronology and useful cross-project insights
sources.text: Date: 17 March 2026; Public repository: Personal AI Employee (https://github.com/omerfarooq223/personal-ai-employee)

ChiefMind (https://github.com/Sobanshahid10/ChiefMind) — Local-first AI personal executive assistant and workflow engine. Soban's project post (https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7495721241899802624/) describes joint work with Umar and names Python 3.11, Flask, Watchdog, Groq, local knowledge retrieval, Gmail API/OAuth, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Playwright, Node/MCP, and supervised launchd/systemd operation. The post and CV describe Gmail monitoring, policy checks, grounded reply drafting, action planning, approval queues before external actions, duplicate/rate protection, execution receipts, audit logs, and a private dashboard. The CV also mentions job discovery. It points to a different repository path, ai-personal-employee (https://github.com/Sobanshahid10/ai-personal-employee), so the relationship between that URL and ChiefMind needs verification.

sources.section: 8. What this corpus can answer, and what it cannot
sources.text: With correct indexing and retrieval, this corpus can answer questions such as: where Umar studied; what the current portfolio says about his teaching and internship experience; which skill domains the portfolio names; what Soban's CV reports as his CGPA and earlier schooling; how Soban describes his automation internship and freelance work; which GitHub projects use YOLO; what evidence the Gemma project reports for its 94.40% result; which projects appear on both accounts; the earliest documented date for Umar's repository projects; how Docinsight and AInsight are related; how many authored commits were observed in the reviewed repository histories; or which source supports a named certification. Every answer should cite the relevant URL or supplied-document identifier and distinguish a source claim from an independently tested fact.

The portfolio lists Urdu (native), English (advanced), and Turkish (basic). These skill levels and language levels are the portfolio's descriptions; project code can corroborate use of a technology but does not by itself certify overall proficiency. Compared with a narrow “AI projects” label, the portfolio explicitly covers full-stack engineering, automation, data systems, security, teaching, and client communication.

sources.section: 3.5 Evidence-backed chronology and useful cross-project insights
sources.text: Evidence and provenance are a repeated design concern. DocuStratum Studio (https://github.com/omerfarooq223/DocuStratum-Studio) keeps DOM-level source links; Gemma Claim Verification (https://github.com/omerfarooq223/gemma-claim-verification) classifies a claim against supplied evidence; PersonaDiff (https://github.com/omerfarooq223/PersonasDiff) retains auditable comparison evidence; and the local Docinsight code ties generated analysis to source passages. This supports the inference that Umar repeatedly builds systems where an answer can be traced back to its input, rather than only producing fluent output.

AutoResearch Agent (https://github.com/omerfarooq223/autoresearch-agent) — Research workflow using Tavily search and LLaMA 3.3 70B via Groq. Its README describes dividing a topic into five sub-questions, parallel searches, synthesis across sources, a self-critique and re-search pass for unsupported claims, credibility notes, and low-confidence flags. It exports PDF, Word, HTML, or Markdown reports with a source appendix. The README says reports typically take 60–120 seconds; this is a project claim rather than a measured guarantee.

The current portfolio certification section (https://omerfarooq223.github.io/#certificates) displays 18 credential entries. It names DataCamp's AI Engineer for Developers Associate, Working with the OpenAI API, Supervised Learning with scikit-learn, and Introduction to AI Agents; Anthropic's AI Fluency: AI Capabilities & Limitations, AI Fluency for Students, Claude 101, Claude Code 101, AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations, Claude Platform 101, and Claude Code in Action; OpenAI Academy's AI Foundations and Applied AI Foundations; Kaggle's Introduction to AI Ethics, 5-Day AI Agents: Intensive Vibe Coding Course, and Machine Learning Explainability; UMT's Peer Tutoring Certificate; and Google's Introduction to Generative AI. The earlier review recorded 16 entries; the live portfolio now shows the two additional DataCamp courses. The portfolio displays certificate images or documents. “Verified” is the portfolio's own label; issuer-side verification was not repeated for every entry.

AI Seekho Day 2026 Gemma fine-tuning hackathon: The portfolio and project repository (https://github.com/omerfarooq223/gemma-claim-verification) report first place. The selected checkpoint is reported at 94.40% accuracy and 94.38% macro-F1 on a 500-example event-day test set. The README describes 472 correct predictions and zero invalid outputs.
